title: Reflected Cosine with Negative Amplitude Coefficient
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: For $y=-2\cos x$, give the amplitude and period and describe the geometric effect of the negative sign.

steps.title: Match the Standard Form
steps.explanation: The outer coefficient is $-2$ and the argument $x$ leaves $B=1$.
steps.why: Keeping track of the sign separately from the magnitude avoids mis-stating amplitude.

steps.title: Take the Absolute Amplitude
steps.explanation: Amplitude measures distance from the midline, so it is $2$ even though the multiplier is negative.

steps.title: Interpret the Reflection and Period
steps.explanation: The minus sign flips the wave: it starts at $y=-2$ at $x=0$ instead of $y=2$, i.e. a reflection across the $x$-axis, while the period stays $2\\pi$.
steps.why: Negating a function reflects its graph across the horizontal axis without changing cycle length.
